title: Jollof rice with chicken
skill: Blended pepper base, cooking rice in the sauce

notes.1: Makes one large pot. The rice cooks evenly only at this size, so make two pots for more.

move.title: Cook the base down, then let the rice drink it
move.body: Jollof rice is cooked at West African family meals, parties, and holidays: rice simmered in a blended sauce of tomatoes, red peppers, and onion until every grain is red and full of flavor. Today you'll blend the base, fry it in oil until it thickens and the oil comes up to the top, then cook the rice in it under a tight lid, while chicken thighs roast in the oven.

callback.body: In spaghetti marinara, you simmered tomatoes until they turned into a thick sauce. Jollof's base cooks down the same way, only longer and thicker, because the rice has to soak up all of it.

why.title: Fry the tomato paste
why.body: Tomato paste stirred in hot oil for a couple of minutes turns darker and sweeter, and loses its raw, tinny taste. It's the deep red at the heart of jollof.

why.title: Cook the base down
why.body: The blended tomatoes and peppers are mostly water. Simmering them until the oil rises to the top cooks that water out, so the flavor gets stronger and the rice doesn't end up soggy.

why.title: Rinse the rice
why.body: Dry rice is coated in loose starch. Rinsed off, the grains cook up separate instead of gluey.

why.title: Seal it and leave it
why.body: Foil under the lid traps the steam, and the steam finishes cooking the rice from the top. Stirring breaks the grains and lets them stick, so the lid stays on.

why.title: Chicken to 165°F
why.body: Chicken is safe to eat when its thickest part reaches 165°F. The thermometer is the only way to know; color can fool you.

wrong.sign: The rice is still hard when the timer rings
wrong.fix: Sprinkle ¼ cup of hot water over the top, seal it again, and cook 5 more minutes on low.
There was too much liquid or it was stirred. Spread it on a sheet pan for a few minutes to dry a little. Next time, cook the base down until the oil shows.

wrong.sign: The bottom is browned and stuck
wrong.fix: Many cooks love that layer. Don't scrape it into the rest; serve the top, then taste the bottom. If it's black and bitter, leave it in the pot.
Serve it with sliced cucumber and plain yogurt on the side. Next time, use half the pepper, or a jalapeño.

quiz.q: Why is the blended base cooked down before the rice goes in?
choices: To cook out the water, so the flavor is strong and the rice isn't soggy
quiz.explain: The oil rising to the top shows it's ready.

quiz.q: Why stay out of the pot once the rice is sealed?
choices: Stirring breaks the grains and the steam escapes
quiz.explain: The trapped steam cooks the top.

quiz.q: How hot must the chicken be inside?
quiz.explain: Checked with a thermometer in the thickest part.

substitutions.note: Milder. Use one, seeds and all.

steps.text: Put a rack in the middle of the oven and heat it to 425°F. Line the sheet pan with foil.

Put the chicken in the large bowl. Add the chicken's oil, curry powder, thyme, garlic powder, and salt, and toss with the tongs until every piece is coated. Spread the pieces on the sheet pan, cover it, and put it in the fridge.
Wash the bowl and tongs in hot, soapy water, then wash your hands with soap for 20 seconds.

Cut the tomatoes and red peppers into big chunks, throwing away the pepper stems and seeds. Peel the onion and cut it in half. Cut one half into chunks; slice the other half thin and keep it for later.
If you're using the Scotch bonnet, an adult cuts it in half and scrapes out the seeds. Use half.
steps.tip: Wash your hands right after touching it, and don't touch your eyes. It burns.

steps.text: Put the tomatoes, red peppers, onion chunks, and Scotch bonnet in the blender. Put the lid on tight and blend until smooth.
steps.tip: Hold the lid down while it runs.

steps.text: Put the rice in the colander and rinse it under cold water, swishing it with your hand, until the water running out is nearly clear. Let it drain.
Heat the base's oil in the large pot over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and cook, stirring, until it's soft.
Add the tomato paste and stir it into the oil for 2 minutes, until it turns a darker red.

Pour in the blended base. Stir in the base's curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, and salt. When it bubbles, turn the heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring every few minutes, until it's thick and the oil comes up to the top.
steps.look: Thick and darker red, with a shiny layer of oil around the edges.
steps.tip: It bubbles and spits. Keep the lid half on, and stir with a long spoon.

steps.text: Pour in the broth and bring it to a boil. Stir in the rice, so it's all under the liquid.
Lay a sheet of foil over the pot, press it down around the edge, and put the lid on top. Turn the heat to low. Don't open it until the timer rings.
Right away, put the chicken in the oven.
With oven mitts, take out the chicken. Push the thermometer into the thickest piece. It needs to read 165°F. If not, roast 3 more minutes and check again.
When the rice timer rings, lift the lid and foil away from you and taste a few grains from the top, after letting them cool a moment. They should be soft all the way through.
steps.look: Red, separate grains, soft with no hard center.
steps.tip: Still hard? Sprinkle ¼ cup of hot water over the top, seal it, and cook 5 more minutes.

steps.text: Turn off the stove and the oven. Take out the bay leaves, fluff the rice with the fork, and serve it with the chicken.

move.title: Toasted in the base, measured by ratio
move.body: This week's skill is cooking a grain by absorption: the rice takes in a measured amount of liquid and nothing is drained. Jollof is the hard case, because the base is part of the liquid. You'll cook the base down to a measured 1½ cups, toast the rinsed rice in it, add exactly 2 cups of broth, and seal the pot so the rice finishes in its own steam.

add.title: The ratio counts the base
add.body: Plain long-grain rice takes about 1½ cups of water for each cup. Cooked longer in a thick sauce, it takes about 1¾, so 2 cups of rice take 3½ cups in all: 1½ cups of cooked-down base and 2 cups of broth. A base left thin carries extra water, and the rice turns soft; that's why you measure it.

add.title: Toast the rice in the base
add.body: Stirred in the hot, oily base for 2 minutes, each grain is coated in fat and its outside starts to cook. Coated grains soak up the liquid evenly and stay separate.

add.title: Rest it sealed
add.body: In 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on, the steam spreads from the wet bottom to the drier top, so the whole pot is even.

wrong.sign: The rice is soft and wet
wrong.fix: The base wasn't cooked down to 1½ cups, so it carried extra water. Spread the rice on a sheet pan for 5 minutes. Next time, measure the base.

wrong.sign: The top is firm and the bottom is soft
wrong.fix: It didn't rest, or the seal leaked. Seal it again and rest 10 minutes off the heat.

wrong.sign: The bottom is browned and stuck
wrong.fix: Leave it in the pot; serve the rice above it. If it's black, the heat was above low. Use the smallest burner next time.

wrong.sign: The chicken reads 165°F at the edge but not the middle
wrong.fix: Check the thickest piece, in its thickest part. Roast 3 more minutes and check again.

choices: It's part of the rice's liquid, so it changes the ratio
To know how spicy it is
So it fits in the blender
quiz.explain: A thin base carries extra water.

quiz.q: How much liquid in all for this jollof's 2 cups of rice?
quiz.explain: About 1¾ cups for each cup of rice, cooked in a sauce.

quiz.q: What does toasting the rice in the base do?
choices: Coats each grain in fat so it cooks evenly and stays separate
quiz.explain: The drill practises the same move.

quiz.q: Why rest the rice sealed off the heat?
choices: The steam evens out the top and bottom

chop.text: Cut the tomatoes and red peppers into 1-inch chunks, throwing away the pepper stems and seeds. Peel and halve the onion. Cut one half into chunks; slice the other half ⅛ inch thick.

pepper.text: Halve the Scotch bonnet with the paring knife, scrape out the seeds and white ribs with the tip, and use half. Wash the knife, the board, and your hands right away.

base.text: Pour in the blended base. Stir in the base's curry powder, thyme, bay leaves, and salt. When it bubbles, turn the heat to medium-low and simmer, stirring every few minutes, until the oil comes up to the top. Pour it into the liquid measuring cup: it should be 1½ cups. More? Pour it back and cook it 5 minutes longer.
base.look: Thick and darker red, with a shiny layer of oil around the edges.

rice.text: Pour the base back into the pot over medium heat. Add the drained rice and stir for 2 minutes, scraping the bottom, so every grain is coated. Pour in the broth and bring it to a boil.

taste-rice.text: When the rice timer rings, turn off the burner and leave it sealed.

add.text: Lift the lid and foil away from you and taste grains from the top and from near the bottom, after letting them cool a moment. Both should be soft all the way through, with no hard center.
add.look: Red, separate grains, the same from top to bottom.
